speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have right groin pain and an abnormal leg position after a rear-end collision. Can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned, and did you hear a popping sound at the moment of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice your right leg turning outward or appearing shorter than the left immediately after the impact? Please confirm if you have any numbness or weakness in the leg.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presentation of a shortened, internally rotated, and adducted leg is classic for a posterior hip dislocation. I need to rule out associated fractures before attempting reduction. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

text: The X-ray confirms a posterior hip dislocation without fracture, which requires immediate reduction to prevent avascular necrosis of the femoral head. I will now proceed with urgent closed reduction under sedation.
